## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
One password validator still needs fixing: the invite flow keeps the old eight-character minimum. The PR body says it raises "the minimum in the password validators", but a password of 8–11 characters is still accepted on that path. Merging as-is would mean the new twelve-character policy is enforced only partly. Within the files this review read, the signup and reset changes and their boundary tests are correct.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/signup.py:1 — correctness — An invited user who sets an 11-character password such as `"x" * 11` is still accepted, because `app/invite.py:1` keeps `MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH = 8` while this change raises signup and reset to 12. `app/invite.py:5` uses the same `len(password) >= MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH` check as the other two validators, so it is clearly a third password validator that the PR body's "raises the minimum in the password validators" should cover. To fix: set `MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH = 12` in `app/invite.py:1`, and change the parametrization in `tests/test_invite.py:6-8` to `[0, 8, 11, 12, 13]` with `length >= 12`, matching the signup and reset tests. — The invite path can still create accounts with passwords shorter than the security policy now requires. That undercuts the stated purpose of the change and leaves an inconsistency that the test suite, as written, accepts.

## Suggestions
(none)

## Strengths
- The updated boundary tests in `tests/test_signup.py:6` and `tests/test_reset.py:6` check 11, 12 and 13, so the inclusive `>=` at the new threshold is tested on both sides.
- Each changed module still has one named constant for its threshold, so the signup and reset changes are each a single line.
